localChanges: chore: update civ1-goody-hut, civ1-barbarians and simple-ai-client

log: `Rules/GoodyHut/barbarians.ts`: civ1-goody-hut's `Barbarians` outcome spawns a horde on the hut's free land neighbours, stepping round them by clamp(4 - cities, 1, 4): up to 3, 4 or 8 units; Horsemen, Swordmen on Mountains (civ-clone/web-renderer#172).

`Rules/Unit/destroyed.ts`: a barbarian Diplomat destroyed by a civilization pays it 100 gold and emits `barbarians:ransom` (player, unit, amount). On `Destroyed`, not `Defeated`, so a leader killed in a stack pays too.
`Rules/City/captured.ts` (Low priority): a city taken by barbarians whose strongest unit on the square attacks at 2 or less is destroyed once the usual capture rules have run.

`Rules/Unit/moved.ts`: a barbarian Horseman, Chariot, Musketman or Cannon leaving a non-city square with Irrigation or a Mine, nearest to a civilization's city, pillages both through the `Pillaged` rules and stops.
civ-clone/web-renderer#171. Depends on civ1-goody-hut, civ1-world, core-goody-hut and core-tile-improvement.
From the clean-context review on this PR:
Ransom: a leader aboard a sunk ship is destroyed as cargo and again in the defeated stack; the rule now checks `!unit.destroyed()`, as civ1-unit's count-loss does, so it pays once.

Burning: every criterion is checked before any rule's effect runs, so a size-1 city shrunk away by civ1-city still passed `!city.destroyed()` and was destroyed a second time. The check is in the effect now.
Burning with no barbarian on the square (`Math.max()` of nothing is -Infinity) no longer burns the city.
A pillager is made inactive as well as out of moves.

The mercenaries outcome becomes v474.05's fourth hut slot: a `Barbarians` outcome when the player has a city and no city of anyone's is within 4 squares, mercenaries otherwise. The `Barbarians` outcome processes the new `Rules/GoodyHut/Barbarians` rule type; the horde itself is spawned by civ1-barbarians, which registers that rule (civ-clone/web-renderer#172).
With no friendly unit within 4 squares, the leader is disbanded once he is (turn % 8) + 4 or more from the nearest city, as v474.05 does; disbanded, so no ransom is paid (civ-clone/web-renderer#171).
